headline_marked: Parliament [[weakened safeguards against enforced disappearance]] in new laws
headline: Parliament weakened safeguards against enforced disappearance in new laws
summary: A former victim of enforced disappearance and current MP warns that new legislation removes critical protections and empowers security forces to investigate themselves.
details: On September 6, opposition MPs protested in the Jatiya Sangsad by wearing black cloths over their mouths and ears to mark the passage of the National Human Rights Commission Bill, 2026, and the Prevention of Enforced Disappearance Act, 2026.
The author, a survivor of enforced disappearance, argues that the new laws effectively 'write deafness into law' by removing the independent oversight that existed in previous ordinances.
Under Section 20 of the new NHRC law, the commission cannot independently investigate security force abuses; it can only request reports from the force's own command.
Section 14 of the enforced disappearance law mandates that complaints go to the ordinary police for investigation, meaning the police—often the perpetrators—are tasked with investigating themselves.

The author highlights a critical flaw: victims' families must identify the specific force responsible before an investigation begins, which is nearly impossible since perpetrators often operate in unmarked vehicles.
This replaces the 2025 ordinances, which featured a judicially chaired selection committee and independent investigators supervised outside police command.
The author calls for the reinstated 2025 ordinances word-for-word and the reappointment of the NHRC commissioners who resigned in protest of the legislative changes.
caption:
A law that requires victims to identify their kidnappers before the state will investigate is not a law against disappearance—it is an enabler.

headline_marked: NBR plans [[fixed monthly VAT for small traders]], starting from ৳500
headline: NBR plans fixed monthly VAT for small traders, starting from ৳500
summary: The National Board of Revenue aims to bring 3-5 lakh small businesses under the VAT net, including those in union-level markets.
details: The National Board of Revenue (NBR) is planning to expand the Value Added Tax (VAT) net to include small-scale traders. Depending on the location, monthly VAT could range from ৳500 for union-level shops to ৳2,000 for district city areas.

Under this plan, ৳1,000 would be charged for traders at the upazila level. To facilitate payments, the NBR intends to allow VAT payments via mobile banking and is considering launching a dedicated app for marginal traders.

This move mirrors the 'package VAT' system used a decade ago, which was abolished in 2019. The NBR is currently collecting data on shops and shopping malls across various upazilas and unions to finalize the list of taxable businesses.

The initiative aims to bring 3 to 5 lakh small businesses into the tax net. Currently, VAT registration is only mandatory for businesses with annual turnover exceeding ৳50 lakh, where a 15% rate typically applies.

The NBR is targeting a total revenue of ৳6.04 lakh crore for the 2026-27 fiscal year, with ৳2.57 lakh crore expected from VAT. Expanding the tax base to small entrepreneurs is a key strategy to meet this target.

Experts suggest that while the move is a positive step for revenue, the implementation will be critical. There are concerns that small traders might be intimidated or may resist paying higher taxes in the future if they get used to a very low fixed rate.
